(2) By means of this writ petition, petitioner has sought quashing of the FIR No. 0170/2024, under Section 376(2)(n), 506 IPC and Section 9(m)/10 of the POCSO Act, registered with PS Lalkuan,
District Nainital.
(3) It is contended by learned Counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is falsely implicated; he is in public life since last more than two decades and there has been no allegation of any wrongdoing against him.

He submits that the FIR is vexatious, aimed at spoiling petitioner's reputation; the incident allegedly occurred on 10.11.2021, however, it was reported to the police on 1.9.2024 and there is no plausible explanation for such huge delay in lodging the FIR.

He relies upon a judgment rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sekaran v. State of Tamilnadu, reported as 2024 (2) SCC 176, for contending that this is a fit case for quashing the FIR within the parameters laid down by Apex Court.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
(2) By means of this writ petition, petitioner has sought quashing of the FIR No. 0170/2024, under Section 376(2)(n), 506 IPC and Section 9(m)/10 of the POCSO Act, registered with PS Lalkuan,
District Nainital.
(3) It is contended by learned Counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is falsely implicated; he is in public life since last more than two decades and there has been no allegation of any wrongdoing against him.
He submits that the FIR is vexatious, aimed at spoiling petitioner's reputation; the incident allegedly occurred on 10.11.2021, however, it was reported to the police on 1.9.2024 and there is no plausible explanation for such huge delay in lodging the FIR.
He relies upon a judgment rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sekaran v. State of Tamilnadu, reported as 2024 (2) SCC 176, for contending that this is a fit case for quashing the FIR within the parameters laid down by Apex Court.
(4) Per contra, Mr. G.C. Lakhchaura, learned Counsel appearing for the complainant, relies upon a judgment rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Punjab v. Gurmit Singh (Criminal Appeal No. 616 of 1986) to contend that in sexual offences, delay in lodging FIR could be due to variety of reasons which concerns the reputation and honour of the family and victim.
He further submits that name/identity of the rape victims should be concealed in order to save them from further embarrassment.

(5) List on 17.9.2024 as fresh.

Petitioner shall neither contact nor influence any witness and he shall report in PS Kotwali, Almora town on each and every day.
(7) Stay application (IA/1/2024) shall be decided on the next date of listing.
